title: A paranormal performance

content:
Senior Kirynn Engelbrecht plays paranormal medium Madame Arcati.

The theatre and dance department is presenting a production of “Blithe Spirit”, Nov. 12-15 at the Oscar Larson Performing Arts Center (OLPAC).

The upcoming production will be shown at 7 p.m. Nov. 12-14, as well as a matinee showing on Nov. 15 at 2 p.m. 

The show follows writer Charles Condomine, who, as research for his book, holds a séance. The  séance accidentally summons the ghost of his late first wife Elvira, who only he is able to see. The play goes on with Elvira attempting to rekindle her relationship with Charles, which Charles’ new wife, Ruth Condomine, does not appreciate. This leads to a dispute between the two wives, while Madame Arcati, a medium, works to resolve the paranormal situation. 

Danika Christopherson, who plays Ruth Condomine describes the show as, “a very witty comedy, about Charles Condomine, an author whose life descends into chaos as he finds himself in a ghostly love triangle.” 

Christopherson hopes that the audience will have a good time at the show and looks forward to seeing their reactions. 

“I’m just very excited to get an audience. We have been running it without an audience for so long, I’m really excited to hear audience reactions,” Christopherson said. “I think theater is very important to let people have a space where they can let go and forget about whatever is happening in their life. So I think just come to the show for a good time.”

The production has not gone without any challenges. The cast experienced some difficulties with the limited amount of time they have had to rehearse the show. 

“We’ve also only had like three and a half weeks to do this, normally we have six, that’s crazy,” Kirynn Engelbrecht, playing Madame Arcati said.

Tickets for the show can be purchased at https://sdstate.evenue.net/events/SUTD-BS, or in person at the OLPAC. Tickets will be available to purchase up until the start of each show, based on ticket availability. Students can get tickets for free with an SDSU ID.
